newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end sharply lower on strong yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end sharply lower on strong yen.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended sharply lower on Monday as the yen's rise against the dollar triggered heavy selling, traders said.

Prices ranged from 250 to 400 yen lower, with the November, January, March and May contracts falling by their 400 yen daily limit at the close. Benchmark July 1998 finished 390 yen weaker at 12,730 yen per tonne.
Since the Chicago grain market was closed on Friday, due to the Independence Day holiday, fluctuations in the dollar/yen rate determined market direction today, traders said.
"Active selling from local investors hit the market particularly in the afternoon," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.43-3/4 per bushel at 0755 GMT, down from $2.44-3/4 at Thursday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean contract was traded at $7.17 per bushel at 0755 GMT, down from $7.22 at Thursday's close.
